sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Treasury withdrawal to reimburse the Ikigai Info governance action deposit.
Recipient: not stated in document; described only as the Ikigai Info governance action submitter or intended recipient

Deliverables: Instant on-chain distribution of 103,000 ADA as part of enactment, Reimbursement of an alleged lost 100,000 ADA governance action deposit, Additional 3,000 ADA compensation for alleged lost staking rewards
Deadline/expiry: Instantly as part of the governance action's enactment on-chain
Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): An Info governance action titled "Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai -" was submitted in September 2024 shortly after the Chang hard fork.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, low materiality): The Ikigai action was symbolic and asked the community to agree with a statement thanking contributors and expressing hope for Cardano's future.

Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, high materiality): A Cardano node bug permitted use of an unregistered stake key in the governance action and caused the submitter to be unable to recover a 100,000 ADA deposit.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposal says there was significant community sentiment that the deposit should be reimbursed because the submitter was an early pioneer of Cardano governance.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposal says entity-based budget submissions did not include the reimbursement once treasury withdrawals became available after the Plomin hard fork.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The Cardano in Oceania initiative included the reimbursement in its budget Info governance action, but that governance action was not approved.
missing: Independent evidence for: A Cardano node bug permitted use of an unregistered stake key in the governance action and caused the submitter to be unable to recover a 100,000 ADA deposit.
Independent evidence for: The proposal says there was significant community sentiment that the deposit should be reimbursed because the submitter was an early pioneer of Cardano governance.
Independent evidence for: The proposal says entity-based budget submissions did not include the reimbursement once treasury withdrawals became available after the Plomin hard fork.
Independent evidence for: The Cardano in Oceania initiative included the reimbursement in its budget Info governance action, but that governance action was not approved.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unsustainable (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "An Info governance action titled "Cardanoの生きがい - Ikigai -" was submitted in September 2024 shortly after the Chang hard fork." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "A Cardano node bug permitted use of an unregistered stake key in the governance action and caused the submitter to be unable to recover a 100,000 ADA deposit." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
